summary.text: Belinda Fox-Spencer, a Constitution Party candidate who describes herself as a health care professional and small business owner, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in West Virginia's 1st District to Carol Miller.
She describes herself as not a career politician and had run for the same seat in 2022 as an independent.

paragraphs.text: Fox-Spencer earned a high school diploma from Peterstown High School, a bachelor's degree from Bluefield State College and a bachelor's degree from Mountain State University.

She says she has 22 years of experience in health care and 32 years in small business; her 2022 campaign website said she is from Monroe County and worked in health care for 20 years as a diagnostic medical sonographer specializing in women's health.

Fox-Spencer filed as an independent candidate on July 15, 2022, after that year's primary, for the redrawn 1st District, and received 10,257 votes (4.5%) in the November 2022 general election won by Carol Miller.
Ballot Access News reported that she was the Constitution Party nominee for the district in the November 3, 2026 general election.
During the campaign, she said she was running on upholding the Constitution, opposing abortion, defending the Second Amendment and energy independence.
She received 3.3% of the vote to Carol Miller's 57.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
